title: Hydrochloric acid
hazards: Causes severe skin burns and eye damage [H314] (concentrated)
Dilute solutions below about 2 M are irritant to eyes
controls: Wear eye protection. Use the lowest concentration that works (often 1 M or less).
Technicians: use a fume cupboard for the concentrated acid.
emergency: Eyes: rinse with gently running water for at least 10 minutes; get medical help.
Spills: dilute and wipe up; neutralise larger spills with sodium carbonate.
disposal: Dilute and pour down the sink.

title: Sodium hydroxide
hazards: Causes severe skin burns and eye damage [H314] (0.5 M and above)
Causes skin and eye irritation [H315/H319] (weaker solutions)
controls: Wear goggles (alkalis are especially harmful to eyes).
Use 0.4 M or weaker where possible.
emergency: Eyes: rinse with gently running water for at least 10 minutes; get medical help.
Skin: rinse with plenty of water.
disposal: Dilute and pour down the sink.

title: Copper(II) sulfate
hazards: Causes skin and serious eye irritation [H315/H319]
controls: Avoid raising dust from the solid; wash hands afterwards.
emergency: Eyes: rinse with water for 10 minutes.
If swallowed: rinse mouth, get medical help.
disposal: Collect solutions for disposal; small amounts of dilute solution can be diluted.

title: Sodium and potassium salts
hazards: Low hazard in normal school use
disposal: Dilute and pour down the sink.

title: Sulfuric(VI) acid
hazards: Causes severe skin burns and eye damage [H314] (1.5 M and above)
Irritant to skin and eyes [H315/H319] (0.5–1.5 M)
controls: Wear goggles; use the lowest concentration that works.
Technicians: always add acid to water, slowly.
emergency: Eyes: rinse with water for at least 10 minutes; get medical help.
Skin: rinse with plenty of water.
disposal: Dilute and pour down the sink.

title: Enzymes
hazards: May cause allergy or asthma symptoms if inhaled [H334]
controls: Technicians make up solutions; students use dilute solutions only.
Do not raise dust or make sprays.
emergency: Breathing difficulty: fresh air, tell the teacher.
disposal: Dilute and pour down the sink.

title: Dyes, indicators and stains
hazards: Some are toxic or irritant; many indicator solutions are made up in flammable ethanol
controls: Use dilute solutions; avoid skin contact (stains hands).
Keep ethanol-based indicators away from flames.
emergency: Eyes and skin: rinse with water.
disposal: Dilute and pour down the sink.

title: Ethanol
controls: No naked flames nearby — heat with a water bath.
Use small volumes; keep bottles closed.
emergency: Fire: smother with a fire blanket; turn off gas.
disposal: Small amounts: dilute with plenty of water.
